'''CZ-D2-9000''' was part of the designation of a [[CZ-series secretary/business communications droid]]<ref name="SC3" /> manufactured by [[Serv-O-Droid, Inc.]]<ref name="Build R2 9" /> During the [[New Republic Era|era]] of the [[New Republic]]<ref name="SC3" /> around [[9 ABY]],<ref name="Date">{{SkeletonCrewDate}}</ref> the [[droid]] was left deactivated on a table<ref name="SC3" /> among an inventory of broken down old droid models in a [[Unidentified droid repair shop|droid repair shop]]<ref name="SC3AD" /> on the [[Silvo's pirates|pirate]]-controlled [[asteroid]] [[Borgo Prime|Port Borgo]].<ref name="SC3" /> 

While searching for the [[pirate]] droid [[SM-33]] in the shop, the fugitive pirate [[Jod Na Nawood]] activated CZ-D2-9000 to learn<ref name="SC3" /> its<ref name="SC3AD" /> name. The droid sat upright and greeted Na Nawood, but as soon as it stated its name and revealed itself to not be SM-33, the pirate deactivated the CZ-series unit and it fell back to the table. CZ-D2-9000 had [[Color|white]] plating and black [[sensor]]s.<ref name="SC3" />

==Behind the scenes==
CZ-D2-9000 appeared in "[[Very Interesting, As an Astrogation Problem]]," the third episode of the [[Disney+]] live-action series ''[[Star Wars: Skeleton Crew]]'',<ref name="SC3" /> which aired on [[December 10]], [[2024]].<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|starwars|status/1861409832349172011|''[[Star Wars]]''|date=2024-11-26|quote=Mark your calendars. 🗓️ On December 2, stream the two-episode series premiere of #SkeletonCrew, only on @DisneyPlus.|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/uxgSx|archivefile=File:StarWars-SkeletonCrewSchedule-Twitter.png}}</ref> The CZ-series prop had previously been created for<ref name="Tarpley interview">{{YouTube|video=ffQnJeotiBU|text=SKELETON CREW Ep3. My Experience|channel=@gordontarpley|name=gordontarpley|date=2024-12-14}}</ref> the [[2018]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|Anthology]] film,<ref name="Solo">''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref> ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'' and was puppetered by [[William Miyamoto]] from beneath the table with [[Mike Senna]] operating the remote control to return its head. There was discussion of swapping out the ''Solo'' model for a more accurate CZ-series costume owned by puppeteer [[Gordon Tarpley]], but, as the other version was already rigged up, there was not time to swap them out.<ref name="Tarpley interview" />
